A device used to establish cohesion within a text

To become snug and comfortable.
To become friendly with.

To undergo creasing; to form wrinkles.

ex.ja: この服はすぐしわになる。

That by which anything is denominated or styled; an epithet; a name, designation, or title; especially, a general name indicating a class…

note.ja: de（完全に）+ nomin（名前）+ ation。名をつけること →「宗派・（貨幣の）単位・名称」。

The result of this process.

note.ja: digest（消化する）+ -ion。di + gerere（運ぶ）。「消化」。

To disprove a discourse, claim or argument.

ex.ja: 解体するの手伝って。

note.ja: dis（取り去る）+ mantle（外套）。「外套をはぐ」→「分解する」。

A ban on trade with another country.
To impose an embargo on trading certain goods with another country.
To impose an embargo on a document.

To look or feel sad, sullen or despondent.

en: Traditionally, a supernatural being of folklore, typically small and grotesque or misshapen, that commonly haunts dark places, often misc…
In later fantasy literature, an evil and grotesquely ugly humanoid, typically powerful and warlike, often associated with orcs and trolls.

goblin.ety: From Middle English gobelyn, from Old Northern French gobelin (compare Norman goubelin, Walloon gobelin), possibly a blend of Old Dutch *kobeholdo (“goblin”) (compare Dutch kabouter, German Kobold) and Late Latin cobalus (“mountain sprite”), from Ancient Greek κόβαλος (kóbalos, “rogue, knave; goblin”). Displaced native Old English pūca from Proto-Germanic *pūkô (“a goblin, spook”), whence English puck.

ex.en: He gave his sudden, goblin like grin.
ex.ja: 彼はいつものように突然不気味な笑みを浮かべた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 gobelin から。ギリシャ語 kobalos（いたずら者）とされる。cobalt と同系。

en: An artillery soldier, especially one who holds private rank.
A person who operates a gun.

note.ja: gun（銃・砲）+ -er。「砲手」。

en: Any of various Old World rodent species belonging to the subfamily Cricetinae.
In particular, a rodent of the species Mesocricetus auratus (the golden hamster) or of a species of the genera Cricetiscus and Phodopus (…
To secrete or store privately, as a hamster does with food in its cheek pouches.

ex.en: My hamster has a swollen testicle on one side.
ex.ja: ハムスターの金玉が片方肥大しています。

note.ja: ドイツ語 Hamster から。古高ドイツ語 hamustro（コクゾウムシ）。食べ物をため込むことから。

Any of several small freshwater polyps of the genus Hydra and related genera, having a naked cylindrical body and an oral opening surroun…

hydra.ety: After the Hydra, from Greek mythology, which grew two new heads every time one of its heads was cut off. The biology sense alludes to the budding method of asexual reproduction that the hydra practices, similar to growing new heads. The figurative sense refers to how the creature could not be killed by a swift, decisive solution (in contrast to a Gordian knot).

note.ja: ギリシャ神話の多頭の水蛇ヒュドラ（Hydra）から。hydōr（水）。

en: Characterized by hypocrisy or being a hypocrite.

hypocritical.ety: From hypocritic + -al, from Ancient Greek ὑποκριτικός (hupokritikós), from ὑποκριτής (hupokritḗs, “actor, hypocrite”), from ὑποκρίνομαι (hupokrínomai, “I play a part on stage”), from ὑπό (hupó, “below”) + κρίνω (krínō, “I choose”).

note.ja: hypocrite（偽善者）+ -ical。ギリシャ語 hypokritēs（役者）。「役を演じる人」→「偽善者」。

en: Admired, distinguished, respected, or well-known.

illustrious.ety: From Latin illūstris (“bright, shining; distinguished, prominent, illustrious”) + -ous (suffix forming adjectives from nouns, to denote possession or presence of a quality in any degree). Illūstris is derived from illūstrō (“to brighten, illuminate; to make famous or illustrious”), from in- (“in, inside”) + lūstrō (“to purify by making a sacrifice; to brighten, illuminate”) (from lūstrō (“purificatory sacrifice”), possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *lewk- (“bright; to shine”) or *lewh₃- (“to wash”)).

note.ja: ラテン語 illustris（明るい・有名な）から。in + lustrum（光）。illustrate、luster と同じ。

A greenish dark blue color; the color of indigo dye.
having a deep purplish-blue colour

indigo.ety: 16th century (as indico, modern spelling from the 17th century), Spanish índigo, Portuguese endego (modern índigo), or Dutch indigo (via Portuguese), all from Latin indicum (“indigo”), from Ancient Greek ἰνδικόν (indikón, “Indian dye”), from Ἰνδία (Indía). ex.ja: 髪に藍染めがついてとれないよ！

ex.en: Indigo blue is one of Japan's traditional colours.
ex.ja: 藍色は日本の伝統色のひとつです。

en: To make timid or afraid; to cause to feel fear or nervousness; to deter, especially by threats of violence.

intimidate.ety: From Medieval Latin intimidātus, perfect passive participle of Latin intimidō (“to intimidate, terrify”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from in- (“in”) + timidus (“afraid, timid”) + -ō (verb-forming suffix); see timid.

en: An instance of being irregular.
The state or condition of being irregular, or the extent to which something is irregular.

irregularity.ety: From Middle French irrégularité, from Medieval Latin irregularitas. Morphologically irregular + -ity.

en: A complicated irregular network of passages or paths, especially underground or covered, in which it is difficult to find one's way.
A maze formed by paths separated by high hedges.
To enclose in a labyrinth, or as though in a labyrinth.
To arrange in the form of a labyrinth.

labyrinth.ety: From Middle English laberynt, laberynthe, from Latin labyrinthus, from Ancient Greek λᾰβύρῐνθος (lăbúrĭnthos, “a maze”).

ex.en: I'd defeated the four sub-bosses and got through the damn long underground labyrinth.
ex.ja: 四天王も倒した、クソ長い地下迷宮もクリアした。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 labyrinthos から。クレタ島のミノタウロスの迷宮。「迷宮」。

Dormancy; the state of being inactive.

note.ja: latent（潜在的な）+ -cy。ラテン語 latere（隠れている）。「潜伏・遅延」。

en: A speculative place or state, thought possibly to be on the edge of the bottomless pit of Hell, where the souls of innocent deceased peop…
Chiefly preceded by in: any in-between place, or condition or state, of neglect or oblivion which results in deadlock, delay, or some oth…
To dance the limbo (etymology 2, noun etymology 2, noun sense 1).
Often followed by under: to pass under something, especially while bending backwards.

limbo.ety:
The noun is derived from Middle English limbo, lymbo (“place where innocent souls exist temporarily until they can enter heaven”), from Latin limbō, the ablative singular of limbus (“border, edge; hem; fringe, tassel”) (notably in expressions like in limbō (“in limbo”) and e limbō (“out of limbo”)); further etymology uncertain, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *lemb- (“to hang limply or loosely”), from Proto-Indo-European *leb- (“to hang down loosely (?)”). Doublet of limp.
The verb is derived from the noun.

note.ja: ラテン語 in limbo（縁に）から。limbus（縁）。天国と地獄の境 →「どっちつかずの状態」。踊りのリンボーは別語。

en: To stay or remain in a place or situation, especially as if unwilling to depart or not easily able to do so.
To remain alive or existent although still proceeding toward death or extinction; to die gradually.

linger.ety: From Middle English lengeren, frequentative of lengen (“to stay, dwell, tarry”), from Old English lenġan (“to lengthen, delay, extend”), from Proto-West Germanic *langijan, from Proto-Germanic *langijaną (compare West Frisian lingje (“to linger”), Dutch lengen, German längen, Icelandic lengja (“to lengthen”)), related to the root of English long. Equivalent to linge or long + -er (frequentative verb suffix).

ex.en: This superstition still lingers on among them.
ex.ja: その迷信は彼らの間で今なお残っている。

ex.en: He lingered in the classroom after school was over.
ex.ja: 彼は授業が終わった後も教室でぶらぶらしていた。

ex.en: The vision that was planted in my senses still silently lingers.
ex.ja: その幻は意識の中に宿り、静寂のなかで動かない。

note.ja: 古英語 lengan（長引かせる）から。long と同系。「ぐずぐず残る」。

en: Insufficient and less than expected of a good thing.
Remarkably bad; of poor quality.

lousy.ety: From Middle English lousy, lowsy, lousi, equivalent to louse + -y.

ex.en: I expect it's his lousy personality that drives off the ladies.
ex.ja: こいつの性根が悪いから非モテなんだろ。

note.ja: louse（シラミ）+ -y。「シラミだらけの」→「ひどい」。

en: A formal meal served in the middle of the day.
A large, cheap, processed sausage served in thin slices.

luncheon.ety:
Of uncertain origin. Possibly derived from an earlier *lumpchin, *lumpchen, a diminutive of lump (“chunk, parcel of food, lunch”), thus related to lunch. It is unclear which came first: whether lunch is a shortening of luncheon, or whether luncheon is an augmentation of lunch. Possibly also a dissimilatory form of or influenced by nuncheon (“light snack taken in the afternoon”).
Noun sense 2 (“sausage”) is likely a ellipsis of luncheon sausage or luncheon meat.

ex.en: We asked ten people to the luncheon.
ex.ja: 昼食会に１０人を招待した。

ex.en: It was a good luncheon, as hotels go.
ex.ja: 世間一般のホテルなみにいえば良い昼食会だった。

ex.en: Is it too early to order from the luncheon menu?
ex.ja: 昼食のメニューの中から注文するには早すぎますか。

note.ja: lunch の古い形とされる。「（正式な）昼食会」。

en: A collection point for mail intended for onward delivery, a secure box or receptacle for this purpose.
A delivery point for mail, a box, compartment or slot for this purpose.

ex.en: There is a mailbox somewhere along this street.
ex.ja: このとおりのどこかに郵便ポストがある。

ex.en: "Where did you find this?" "In the mailbox."
ex.ja: 「これ、どこにあったの？」「ポストだよ」

ex.en: I found your letter in the mailbox.
ex.ja: あなたからの手紙が郵便受けに入ってたよ。

soprano.ety: Borrowed from Italian soprano, from Vulgar Latin *superānus, adjective from preposition Latin super (“above”). Doublet of sovereign, from the same Latin root via Old French.

ex.en: She is famous as a soprano.
ex.ja: 彼女はソプラノ歌手として有名だ。

ex.en: She is famed as a soprano.
ex.ja: 彼女はソプラノ歌手として有名だ。

ex.en: I was a better alto but was selected as a mezzo-soprano.
ex.ja: わたしはアルトの方が良かったんだけど、メゾソプラノに入れられた。

note.ja: イタリア語 soprano（上の）から。sopra（上に）、ラテン語 supra。「最高音部」。super と同じ。

en: A computer application for organization, analysis, and storage of data in tabular form.
A document created with such an application.
To model or compute by means of a spreadsheet.

ex.en: Once you get the hang of it, spreadsheet software is really useful.
ex.ja: 表計算ソフトは、覚えておくと何かと便利よ。

note.ja: spread（広げる）+ sheet（紙）。広げた大きな帳簿 →「表計算ソフト」。

zh: 停滯不前的 /停滞不前的

en: Lacking flow or motion, and thus usually not fresh or healthy; decaying through stillness.
Without activity, change or progress, or excitement in an unhealthy manner; inactive, stale.

stagnant.ety: From French stagnant, from Latin stagnans, present participle of stagno (“to form a pool of standing water”).

note.ja: ラテン語 stagnans（よどんでいる）から。stagnum（池）。stagnation と同じ。

en: A tough band of flexible but inelastic fibrous collagen tissue that connects a muscle with its bony attachment and transmits the force wh…
The hamstring of a quadruped.

tendon.ety: Borrowed from French tendon or Medieval Latin tendō, from Ancient Greek τένων (ténōn, “sinew, tendon”), modified by association with the verb tendō (“to stretch”). Compare Middle English thenoun.

note.ja: ラテン語 tendere（伸ばす）から。筋肉と骨をつないで張るもの →「腱」。

en: Resistance to fracture when stressed, or the degree of such resistance.
Fortitude; hardiness; mettle.

toughness.ety: From Middle English toughnesse, towghnesse, towghenesse, equivalent to tough + -ness.

note.ja: tough + -ness。

en: That has not been answered or addressed.

unanswered.ety: From Middle English unansuered, unanswerd, equivalent to un- + answered.

ex.en: What unanswered questions remain?
ex.ja: 未回答の質問は、どんなものが残ってる？

note.ja: un（否定）+ answered（答えられた）。

en: Breaching the established standards of conduct or behavior within a particular organization or profession.
Immoral, morally wrong.

unethical.ety:

ex.en: It's unethical to own a cat as a pet.
ex.ja: 猫を飼うのは不倫理的だよ。

note.ja: un（否定）+ ethical（倫理的な）。ethics と同じ。

en: The residential part of a city, which is usually away from the central business district.
The commercial center of town (in Charlotte, North Carolina).
In the upper part of a town.
Of or relating to an affluent area or population.
To or in the upper part of a town.

note.ja: up（上の方）+ town。マンハッタン北部（地図の上）から。downtown の対。

en: Of, relating to, occurring in, or affecting urine, its production, function, or excretion.
Of, relating to, occurring in, or affecting the organs involved in the production, function, or excretion of urine.

urinary.ety: From New Latin ūrīnārius. By surface analysis, urine + -ary.

ex.en: I have a urinary problem.
ex.ja: 排尿障害があります。

note.ja: urine（尿）+ -ary。ラテン語 urina。

en: Possessing or showing courage or determination; brave, heroic.
Characterized by or done with bravery or valour.

valiant.ety: From Middle English vailaunt (“having or showing courage or valour, valiant; characterized by valour; powerful, strong; person of valour or strength; excellent, worthy; beneficial, useful; valuable; legally valid, binding”) [and other forms], from Anglo-Norman vaillaunt, vaylant [and other forms], and Old French vailant, vaillant (“brave, valiant; having value, valuable”) [and other forms], from the present participle of valoir (“to have value; to be worth”), from Latin valēre (“to have value; to be worth; to be strong; to have influence or power”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂welh₁

note.ja: 古フランス語 vaillant（強い）から。ラテン語 valere（強い）。「勇敢な」。valor、valid と同じ val。

zh: 治安會會員 /治安会会员

en: A member of a vigilance committee.
A person who acts outside of legal authority, often violently, to punish or avenge a crime, right a perceived wrong, etc.

vigilante.ety: Borrowed from Spanish vigilante (“watchman, guard”), from Latin vigilans. Doublet of vigilant.

note.ja: スペイン語 vigilante（見張り）から。ラテン語 vigilare（目を覚ましている）。「自警団員」。vigilant と同じ。

en: A venomous snake in the family Viperidae.
Any venomous snake.

viper.ety: From Middle French vipere, from Old French vipre, from Latin vīpera, contracted from vīvipara f (“viviparous”, adj.), from vīvus (“alive”, adj.) + parere (“to bear”, verb). Doublet of weever and wyvern.

note.ja: ラテン語 vipera ＝ vivus（生きた）+ parere（産む）。卵ではなく子を産むと考えられたことから。

en: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday, but not Saturday or Sunday.
Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, but not Friday.

weekday.ety: Inherited from Middle English wykeday, from Old English wicdæġ (“weekday”), from Proto-West Germanic *wikadag, from Proto-Germanic *wikadagaz (“weekday”). By surface analysis, compound of week + day. Compare West Frisian wikedei (“weekday”), Dutch weekdag (“weekday”), German Low German Wekendag (“weekday”), German Wochentag (“weekday”), Danish ugedag (“weekday”), Swedish veckodag (“weekday”), Norwegian ukedag (“weekday”), Faroese vikudagur (“weekday”), Icelandic vikudagur (“weekday”).

ex.en: The weekdays are: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday.
ex.ja: 平日は、月火水木金です。

ex.en: She is always busy on weekdays.
ex.ja: 彼女の平日はいつも忙しい。

ex.en: Weekdays Monday through Friday, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
ex.ja: 月曜日から金曜日の平日の間、午前9時から午後5時までです。

note.ja: week（週）+ day（日）。「平日」。

en: A small furrow, ridge or crease in an otherwise smooth surface.
A line or crease in the skin, especially when caused by age or fatigue.
To make wrinkles in; to cause to have wrinkles.
To pucker or become uneven or irregular.

wrinkle.ety: From Middle English wrinkle, wrynkel (“crease, fold, wrinkle”), from the verb (see below). Cognate with Dutch wrinkel (“wrinkle, crease”). Compare also Middle English runkel (“wrinkle”), from Old Norse hrukka (“wrinkle”), from Proto-Germanic *hrunkwǭ (“wrinkle, crease”), whence also French fronce (“crooked smile, scowl, frown”), German Runzel (“wrinkle”), Danish rynke (“wrinkle”), Swedish rynka and rynkla (“wrinkle”).

ex.en: His blue coat was dirty and wrinkled.
ex.ja: 彼の青いコートは汚れていてしわくちゃだった。

ex.en: I ironed out the wrinkles in my pants.
ex.ja: 私はズボンのしわをアイロンで伸ばした。

ex.en: She has started to get a few wrinkles around her eyes.
ex.ja: 彼女の目の回りには、小じわができてきた。

note.ja: 古英語 gewrinclod（ねじれた）から。wrench と同系。「しわ」。

en: The act of abstracting, separating, withdrawing, or taking away; withdrawal; the state of being taken away.
The taking surreptitiously for one's own use part of the property of another; purloining.

abstraction.ety: From Middle English abstraccyone; either from Middle French abstraction or from Medieval Latin abstrāctiō (“separation”), from Latin abstrahō (“draw away”). Equivalent to abstract + -ion.

note.ja: abs（離れて）+ tract（引く）+ ion。具体物から引き離すこと →「抽象（化）・放心状態」。

en: An appendage; something attached to something else in a subordinate capacity.
A person associated with another, usually in a subordinate position; a colleague.
Connected in a subordinate function.
Added to a faculty or staff in a secondary position.
To work as an adjunct professor.

adjunct.ety: From Latin adiunctus, perfect passive participle of adiungō (“join to”), from ad + iungō (“join”). Doublet of adjoint.

note.ja: ラテン語 adjunctus（結びつけられた）から。ad + jungere（結ぶ）。junction、join と同じ。

en: To move upward, to fly, to soar.
To slope in an upward direction.

ascend.ety: From Middle English ascenden, borrowed from Old French ascendre, from Latin ascendō (“to go up, climb up to”), from ad (“to”) + scandō (“to climb”); see scan. Unrelated to accede other than common ad prefix.

ex.en: This mountain path ascends to the beautiful lake.
ex.ja: この山道を登ると美しい湖に出る。

ex.en: The smoke ascended into the air.
ex.ja: 煙は空中へと舞い上がった。

ex.en: The road ascends to the village.
ex.ja: 道は上り坂になってその村に出る。

note.ja: a（〜へ）+ scend（登る）。上へ登る →「上る・昇進する」。descend（下る）と対。
